papers.title: Trial by Trace: Benchmarking AI Agent Harnesses for Reliability and Failure Attribution
papers.abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used to solve real-world problems, and their effectiveness depends on both the underlying models and the harnesses that support their operation. However, most existing benchmarks focus on model capabilities and overall agent performance, with limited attention to the evaluation ofagent harnesses. To address this gap, we introduceTraceTrial-Bench, which organizes harness reliability into seven components covering context, execution, governance, lifecycle, observability, tools, and verification. We construct 95 expert-level, mechanism-oriented tasks with executable or state-based ground truth to support semantically equivalent comparisons while preserving the native behavior of each harness. We design aTrajectory Tracing(TT) module to capture agent execution traces and introduce atwo-layer evaluation frameworkthat separately assesses agent performance and harness reliability. In addition, we design aMulti-source Evidence Acquisition(MEA) module to provide evidence from the agent context, harness, and execution environment for LLM-based evaluation, and develop aFailure Attribution(FA) module that uses explicitmechanism chainsto support attribution at the run level. Across 4 harnesses, 9 models, and 95 tasks, our evaluation of 3,420 runs yields macro-averaged harness scores ranging from 59.8% to 72.0%, while 31.1% of runs achieve task success despite failing at least one harness criterion.TraceTrial-Benchprovides an auditable and reproducible foundation for comparingagent harnesses, diagnosing their failures, and studying how harness design interacts with model behavior.

papers.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
papers.abstract: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited.Video world modelscan capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweightPhysical Dynamics Moduleextractsphysical tokensfrom vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns through direct prediction of future RGB, depth, andoptical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision through a frozen pretrained video world model. Training relies entirely on publicly available data, expanded throughhuman-to-robot synthesis,subtask annotation, andembodied chain-of-thought(ECoT) annotation. Across four simulation benchmarks, PDRVLA achieves success rates of 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin~2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv. Ablations show improved future prediction with world-model supervision and evaluate how subtask conditioning, future object-pose supervision, and ECoT training affect action success.

papers.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
papers.abstract: Interactive world generationrequires models to follow successive commands while preserving relevant history and action consequences. We present Hy-Nomas, avideo world modelwith an 8Bdiffusion backbonethat supports free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple interaction turns. It generates variable-length segments conditioned on current inputs and cached history. Our central design aligns structured video captions with action-awarecausal attention: descriptive context remains accessible across segments, while action instructions are restricted to their intended temporal windows. Avision-language Prompt Enhancer(PE) translates user requests and multimodal interaction histories into structured conditions for the next segment. A multi-stage curriculum progressively introduces causal generation, text interaction, camera control, and training on model-generated histories, followed bydiffusion distillation. In human evaluation, Hy-Nomas shows superior performance over existing world models. We release model weights, code and benchmarks, together with a lightweight adaptation workflow, to support reproducible research oninteractive world generation.

papers.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
papers.abstract: Asfoundation modelsevolve from information generation to digital work execution, agents are increasingly capable of completing complex tasks across tools, applications, and workflows. However, existing research lacks a unified perspective on how agents reliably accomplish delegated work. To address this gap, we present a work-centric, system-level perspective that viewswork agentsas systems combiningfoundation modelsandruntime harnessesto execute tasks instateful workspacesand deliver verifiable outcomes. We introduce two complementary dimensions,work persistenceandwork openness, to characterize working conditions, and classify digital work into five forms according to task scope and organization. Building on this framework, we identify five core capability families required for reliable work execution and examine approaches tomodel optimization,harness optimization, and theirjoint optimization. We further analyze existing evaluation methods and metrics from the perspective ofwork outcomes. Finally, we discuss future research directions, including sustained work delegation, adaptation to open environments, and the interaction between work execution and capability improvement. This paper provides a unified framework for understanding, optimizing, and evaluatingwork agents, supporting the development of systems capable of delivering reliable, verifiable, and practically valuablework outcomes.

papers.title: OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images
papers.abstract: Generating videos of a specific subject from a few reference images remains challenging when the camera reveals surfaces that are not visible in the input. Earlysubject-to-video(S2V) methods condition on a single reference image and must therefore infer the subject's unseen appearance and geometry as the viewpoint changes. To address this limitation, recent methods extend S2V to multiple reference views, providing more information about the subject from different viewpoints. However, they do not explicitly specify the 3D structure that connects these observations. In addition, existing training data do not guarantee that viewpoint changes preserve the same underlying 3D subject. We present OmniShowcase, built on two components: (i) a fully automateddata synthesis pipelinethat produces training videos along diversecamera trajectories, with viewpoint variation driven by underlying subject geometry, even spanning full 360-degree orbits; and (ii) ageometry-conditioningmethod that provides the video model with a turntable ofsurface-normal mapsreconstructed from the reference views without requiring temporal alignment with the generated frames. We construct Showcase-4K, a corpus of 3D-asset-based videos covering twelve camera motions across 88 trajectory configurations with reconstruction-derived surface-normal conditioning, and ShowcaseBench, a held-out evaluation set with the source meshes and camera parameters used to render each video. Experiments show state-of-the-art subject identity and3D consistencywhile maintaining competitive video quality and motion. Project page: justin4ai.github.io/OmniShowcase

papers.title: Efficient Streaming Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction for Real-World Acoustic Scenes
papers.abstract: Streamingaudio-visual target speaker extraction(AVTSE) is essential for latency-sensitive applications. However, current causal systems face two coupled gaps. First, standard benchmarks fix the number of speakers at two and ignore the near-/far-field interference, reverberation, and sudden noise of real scenes. Second, high-performance causal architectures are too heavy for edge deployment. Lightweight alternatives try to reclaim capacity by repeatedly invoking a small separator, which offsets the savings. To address the first gap, we releaseRealSSA, a realistic AVTSE benchmark consisting ofRealSSA-Sim andRealSSA-Real.RealSSA-Sim provides controllable simulated scenes with 1--5 dynamic near-field interfering speakers; scenes with far-field interference additionally include 10--15 far-field interfering speakers.RealSSA-Real provides a held-out real-recorded evaluation set. To address the second gap, we proposeFalcon, acausal AVTSEmethod. Its Separator performsmulti-scale time-frequency separationin a single encoder--decoder pass. We trainFalconwith anencoder-space speaker contrastive loss. This loss suppresses near-field leakage at zero inference cost and transfers across backbones.Falconachieves state-of-the-art extraction quality onRealSSA-Sim, LRS2-2Mix, LRS3-2Mix, and VoxCeleb2-2Mix. Compared with the causal AV-TFGridNet baseline, it cuts parameters by 91.9%, computation by 20.2 times, and GPU inference latency by 11.1 times. Code and demo are available at https://cslikai.cn/Falcon/.

papers.title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
papers.abstract: Vision-language modelsare shifting from offline passive understanding toward onlineproactive interaction. However, prevailing methods largely rely on explicit requests while miss theimplicit user intent(e.g., "where should I click next?" while a user navigate a website), meanwhile fail to update the state simultaneously as user requests might update continuously. These limitations make them less suited to intent-aware interaction in practical. To address these challenges, we introduceStreamVibe-Bench, a new benchmark serving as testbed for user intent interaction, with 4.1K evaluation samples and 85K training samples spanning explicit, implicit, anddynamic intents. Building on this benchmark, we developStreamVibe-VL, astreaming proactive modelthat infersimplicit user intents from continuous observations and dynamically tailors its interactions as these intents evolve. We further introduceStreamVibe-Harness, which maintains user intents as persistent states with a fleixble lifecycles via ahierarchical memoryto track the latest user intent and environmental state. Our experiments reveal three key findings: (i)StreamVibe-VLpreserves strong general video understanding while improving response timing and answer quality by 10.7% over other baselines; (ii) existing proactive models remain limited in understanding user intent and deciding when to respond, especially under implicit anddynamic intents; and (iii)StreamVibe-Harnessfurther improves response consistency and adaptation over sustained interaction, resulting in a 12.3% gain inproactive interaction.

papers.title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs
papers.abstract: Diffusion vision-language models(DVLMs) process their entire input at every denoising step. Since visual tokens make up 89-97% of this input on the benchmarks we study, most of the decoding computation is spent repeatedly processing the same image.Visual token pruningmethods partially relieve this burden by removing part of the visual tokens, but they lose the removed information and still process the remaining image at every step. To measure how often the image is actually needed, we compareLLaDA-V's predictions with and without the image at every decoding step and find that removing the image changes a token being unmasked at only 22.8% of steps on average and at as few as 7.9%. We therefore proposeLOWN, a decoding method that decides at every step whether to process the image and how many tokens to unmask.LOWNpredicts themasked tokenswithout the image and processes the image only when this prediction disagrees with the last image-conditioned prediction. Agreement certifies the earlier prediction for reuse, and the number of certified tokens sets how many are unmasked in that step. We further observe that the need for the image differs across benchmarks, soLOWN's adaptive decision is needed rather than a fixed schedule. Without training or a tuned threshold,LOWNretains 99.6% ofLLaDA-V's score on ten benchmarks at 35.3% of thedecoding FLOPson average.LOWNalso generalizes across LLaDA-based DVLMs, composes orthogonally withvisual token pruning, and runs underkey-value cachingfor further efficiency gains. Code and project page are available at https://hyeon9698.github.io/LOWN/

papers.title: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systemsoften rely on predefined collaboration structures, limiting their ability to adapt to diverse task requirements. We introduce DynaFlow, a framework that integrates free-formexecutable workflow synthesisinto the action space of the main agent. The agent decides when collaboration is needed and generates task-specific programs that coordinatesub-agentsthrough sequential or parallel execution, structured information exchange, and verification. Execution results and traces inform subsequent actions, enabling the agent to adapt collaboration as reasoning progresses. We train only the main agent throughsupervised fine-tuningon distilled trajectories, followed by refinement on examples filtered for unsupported premises, biased verification, and information-flow defects. Allsub-agentsremain fixed, separatingorchestrationlearning from executor capability improvement. Across six benchmarks spanning mathematical reasoning, scientific question answering, and multi-hop retrieval, DynaFlow achieves 88.08% overall accuracy in Forced mode, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 10.90 percentage points with the same Qwen3.5-27B backbone. Workflow analysis finds more explicit use, verification, and refinement of upstream outputs after training, highlightingcross-stage information flowas a key dimension of multi-agentorchestration.

papers.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
papers.abstract: Memory is increasingly used inlong-horizon agents, yet the net value of building memory over direct retrieval from raw history remains largely unclear. Through a large-scale evaluation across multiple benchmarks and model backbones, we find many dedicated memory systems underperform naiveRAGin many cases, indicating a negative net value. TakingRAGas a reference, we dissect the net value of memory into the gains and losses over direct retrieval, termedmemory benefitandmemory tax. These gains and losses arise because memory process changes how the raw information is organized and accessed. We view such changes as the double-edged deviations from the raw history. They are originally designed and introduced to benefit the task, for example by reorganizing facts or distilling preferences, but some may also remove or obscure evidence, giving rise tomemory tax. Sincememory benefitreflects the expected gains of its design, we then focus more on the overlookedmemory tax, study how it arises from the system and evaluation side, and generalize the concept to more application scenarios of memory. We hope the notion ofmemory taxcan provide a new lens and shift more attention from standalone performance to the net value of memory, informing more reliable memory designs and evaluations. We will open-source the code and results to the community. Project Page: https://hexuan21.github.io/MemoryTax/

papers.title: HABIT-Bench: Evaluating Habit Induction from Longitudinal Weak Evidence in Agent Memory
papers.abstract: In long-term interactions with large language model (LLM) agents, users reveal habits through their choices and actions. These habits capture implicit user information that agents must infer across conversations. However, individual observations may provide only partial evidence about a habit or when it applies. Retaining past interactions alone does not ensure that agents can infer habits and apply them appropriately. We introduceHABIT-Benchto evaluate how wellagent memory systemsinfer habits from weak evidence and apply them to later requests. We construct synthetic user histories fromtask-oriented dialoguedata and controlledhabit graphs. The histories span hundreds of sessions across food, finance, software, and travel. Four-choice tasks assess agents' ability to infer user habits and apply them appropriately. They includetemporary exceptions, changes in habits, and suggestions that users have not accepted. Sampled tasks undergo independent human review. We evaluate eight memory methods with Qwen3-235B-A22B and GLM-5.3-Flash. The best-performing memory method achieves 33.61\%macro accuracyacross the four domains. Performance remains limited even when annotated evidence is supplied directly. These results expose a persistent gap between access to past interactions and the ability to infer and appropriately use user habits.

papers.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned world modelsoffer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. However, existing world-model-based methods largely treat world models as forward-only surrogates of the physical environment, leaving untapped a capability no physical environment affords: rewinding to past decision points to explorecounterfactual futures. We introduceRollback, a policy improvement paradigm that turns world models from passive simulators into counterfactual engines: it rolls back to critical decision points, branches into alternative actions, and contrasts their outcomes to attribute success to individual decisions. This concentrates imagination where it matters most and distills counterfactual outcomes into fine-grained, action-level supervision without a separately learned value model. We build a scalable training system that unifies distributedworld-model searchwith asynchronous real-robot execution, forming a self-reinforcing cycle: real-world experience continually sharpens the world model, and a sharper world model in turn drives further policy improvement. We term the world-model side of this cycletest-time physics grounding, a capability that hand-built physics simulators lack: while the world model serves as the training environment, real transitions from the policy it trains correct its dynamics through a lightweightLoRApipeline. Experiments on three challenging real-world tasks show thatRollbackimproves success rates over the strongest baseline by an absolute 10.67%, 11.11%, and 11.85% on block extraction, ball tossing, and tabletop curling, respectively, while achieving more stable improvement throughout training. Although initialized from teleoperated demonstrations far below human level,Rollbacksurpasses the average success rate of human players on both ball tossing and tabletop curling within 8 hours of training.

papers.title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Training aspatial VLMto answer which side an object lies on does not require it to preserve the metric displacement that determines that answer, while supervision for a distance estimate may leave categorical relations largely unconstrained. When post-training emphasizes one readout, improvements can therefore concentrate on that interface while transfer to others remains weak or even degrades; we call this observed specializationinterface lock-in.ChronoReplayaddresses it by replaying heterogeneous spatial supervision as chronologically ordered episodes, retaining source-native targets, and balancing supervision across families. Under the same observation access, a singleChronoReplaycheckpoint improvesOVO-S-Bench,OST-Bench, andUCS-Benchtogether, including a 13.41-point gain onOST-Bench, and achieves the highest three-benchmark mean among the supervision settings compared here. Same-data controls further separate the ingredients of this transfer: answer serialization redistributes gains across OST and UCS, family-balanced learning improves over ordinaryjoint SFTand natural turn weighting, and chronological replay exceeds a shifted-order control by about 2.41 OST points across two paired seeds.Adaptive frame selectionthen changes evidence access while keeping the trained model fixed, providing an additional inference-time gain at lower visual cost. Streaming spatial performance depends on what distinctions supervision preserves, how heterogeneous histories are organized during learning, and what causal evidence inference makes available at test time.

papers.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
papers.abstract: People have long dreamed of an assistant that is always there to guide them and remind what they forget, from new dishes to lost keys. Powered bymultimodal large language models(MLLMs),egocentric AI assistantson wearable devices are bringing this dream within reach: they see what the user sees and give instructions for user's physical work when necessary. However, testing such assistance is challenging and usually requires real people. The expensive and rare real interaction data leaves a key question unanswered: Can today's MLLMs truly help people in physical world? To answer this question, we proposeInteractiveWorld, the first verifiable environment forclosed-loop interactionbetween human and AI assistant. Unlike existing robot-centric simulators,InteractiveWorldlets the assistant guide a human agent who observes the scene, understands instructions, and acts independently. It thus realistically simulates how AI assistant collaborates with human: the assistant instructs, the human acts, and the environment executes actions and updates what they see next. Building on it, we introduceInteractiveBench, the first dynamic benchmark foregocentric AI assistants, with 120 multi-turn tasks across six categories. In each task, the assistant guides the human in real time, and every instruction shapes the outcome, which is scored by verifiable,state-based rewards. Experiments with 12frontier MLLMsshow they are still far from reliable assistants. Even the strongest model, Claude Fable 5.1, achieves at most 20% and 25% on long-horizon Guidance and Planning tasks, respectively. Overall, our work offers a verifiable platform and a rigorous evaluation set, laying a solid foundation for research on interactive MLLM assistants that truly help people in the physical world.

papers.title: Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities
papers.abstract: We present Youtu-Parsing-Omni, anomni-modal parserthat converts documents, images, audio, and video into structured records grounded in space and time, providing a perception layer for agents that read, locate, and cite evidence across modalities. Its design rests on one encoder for every modality and one schema for every task. Youtu-Omni-Encoder, initialized from a pre-trained language model to strengthen text reading, encodes all modalities withshared weightsin a unified space-time coordinate system, and a few fusion layers let video frames attend to concurrent audio, bringingcross-modal fusionandtemporal alignmentinto perception itself. OmniSchema unifies the outputs of all ten parsing tasks, allowing a singleself-evolving post-trainingprocedure, OmniSchema-AwareOn-Policy Distillation(OSAD), to provide a shared token-role-based objective across tasks. In each round, the model is trained on its own rollouts againsttoken-level targetsfrom a reference-conditioned copy of itself, which is then refreshed with the trained weights, so that the parser and its supervision co-evolve. With a single 5 B-parameter checkpoint, Youtu-Parsing-Omni achieves state-of-the-art performance on OmniDocBench v1.6 (96.96 Overall) and leads all open-weight models on OmniParsingBench (75.08 Avg.), with its advantage concentrated on audio and video. It also achieves the best overall chart-parsing score (95.02) and the highest exact chemical-fingerprint agreement among compared systems, and matches a dedicated optical-music model in character-level transcription of typeset sheet music while staying far ahead of general-purpose systems. Code and model weights are publicly available.

papers.title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving
papers.abstract: Agentic services alternate between model inference on clustered GPUs and external tools on distributed CPUs. In this scenario, existing systems (1) overlooktool-return readinessin service evaluation, wasting limited resources, and (2) use heuristic strategies to decideadmission and placementon GPUs, resulting in suboptimal scheduling decisions. To bridge this gap, we present TAO, a tool-aware joint scheduling framework forLLM-based agentic serving. Its value interface combines near-term tool readiness,node-specific cache creditwithtime-aware decay, andtoken footprint; a dynamic program jointly selects and places waiting sessions under capacity constraints. Across the 12 reported model-workload-concurrency settings, TAO reduces latency by up to 26.8%, reduces meantime to first token (TTFT)by up to 36.3%, and increasesdecode throughputby up to 29.5% relative to the best evaluated state-of-the-art baseline for each metric.

papers.title: A-RSI: Adaptive Task Refresh for Zero-Data Multimodal Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Recursive self-improvementrequires models not only to acquire useful training experience, but also to decide when their current experience has ceased to be useful. Existing methods often focus on what experience to generate next, while paying less attention to when fresh experience should be introduced. Many also construct training targets throughself-consistencyor majority voting, making supervision depend on the model's own uncertain predictions. We address these two questions separately:training dynamicsdetermine when to acquire new experience, while the answers to new tasks remain independently checkable.A-RSImonitorsreward variationand accuracy in training logs to refresh atask poolwhen its learning signal declines, without consulting validation or test scores. A static library ofmodel-authored programsproducesmultimodal questionsand derives their reference answers; we specify the task-generation contract, automatically verify chosen properties of the reward and refresh rules, and separately audit the generated answers. The training loop uses no external training examples or human-written answer labels. On the primary eleven-benchmark suite,A-RSIraises the performance average from 57.77 to 61.05 with 800 fresh tasks.

papers.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. We introduce ThinkWorld, a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning inworld dynamicsand strengthens it throughreinforcement learningwithworld imagination. ThinkWorld represents each action thought as aChain-of-Dynamics(CoD), a sequence of discretemotion tokensthat captures the intermediate dynamics connecting the current world to a future state and serves as a common action representation across embodiments. We first initialize CoD with action-labeled demonstrations, then predict the future induced by each CoD and reinforce those whose predictions better match the observed outcome. This enables videos without action annotations to provide direct supervision from observed state transitions, allowing human and robot experience to refine the same reasoning space. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate effective human-to-robot transfer and strong generalization to unseen tasks and environments.

papers.title: UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents
papers.abstract: Agentic recommendationpursues shopper goals through sequences of context-dependent decisions. Developing and evaluating such policies requires faithfulrecommendation world modelsthat capture both the interactive shopping environment and users' behavioral responses over long interactions. Existing resources rarely provide long-horizon, fine-grained real-user trajectories or support trajectory-level evaluation andoffline validationagainst production A/B results. We introduceUserArena, a real-world e-commerce interactive benchmark containing 64,729 session trajectories from 11,010 users, spanning 566,102 items and 13 action types.UserArenapairs these trajectories with aninteractive environmentand supportsoffline validationagainst outcomes from a controlled production A/B test, enabling five-level evaluation from output validity and local decisions to sequential behavior, personalization, and outcomes. To improvesimulator fidelityover these long-horizon interactions, we further proposeOn-Policy Trajectory Distillation(OPTD), which usestrajectory-level intentto provide dense teacher targets on student-generated rollouts. Experiments show that OPTD achieves the strongest overall fidelity among the evaluated simulators underUserArena's evaluation protocol and most closely reproduces the production policy effect in offline simulation.

papers.title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
papers.abstract: Whether models trained on different modalities converge to the same representation of the world is central to AI. ThePlatonic Representation Hypothesis(PRH) conjectures that they do as they scale, but without a proof it offers neither a guarantee nor a recipe. We turn the hypothesis into a theorem. First, we prove a Platonic Representation Theorem:Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures(JEPAs) trained separately on any number of modalities learn the same representation up to one rotation whenever theirpositive pairsare two observations of one scene--good views--and their misalignment is bounded otherwise. Second, we show thatnext-token predictionis a JEPA with bad views, parts of a single document, which explains why language models align with vision only through scale. Third, we validate the theory from 145k captions to the texts of 940M web images, and uncover ascaling law of alignmentthat predicts unseen runs within seed noise.Good viewsneed 42 times fewer training samples thannext-token predictionon the same corpus to reach the same alignment, and a 109M-parametertext JEPAaligns withDINOv2andCLIP's image encoders better than every language model we evaluated, up to 72B parameters, and thanCLIP's text encoder:next-token predictionis a remarkably inefficient route to platonic representations. As a showcase, one rotation turns separately trained encoders into an image captioner (CIDEr .838 on COCO). Even that rotation needs no pair: on the latest pair-free benchmark, ourtext JEPAbeats every zero-shot accuracy reported with language models up to 8B parameters, e.g., 64\% against at most 56\% top-5 on ImageNet-100. Positive views, and not scale alone, are thus the lever to build platonic representations.
